source_text: Ubi tunc Marcion, ponticus nauclerus, stoicae studiosus? Ubi Valentinus platonicae sectator? Nam constat illos, neque adeo olim fuisse, Antonini fere principatu, et in catholicae primo doctrinam credidisse apud Ecclesiam romanensem, sub episcopatu Eleutherii benedicti, donec ob inquietam semper eorum curiositatem, qua fratres quoque vitabant semel et iterum ejecti, Marcion quidem cum ducentis sestertiis quae Ecclesiae intulerat, novissime in perpetuum discidium relegati, venena doctrinarum suarum disseminaverunt. Postmodum idem Marcion, poenitentiam confessus cum conditioni datae sibi occurrit, ita pacem recepturus, si caeteros quos perditioni erudisset, Ecclesiae restitueret, morte praeventus est. Oportebat enim haereses esse. Nec tamen ideo bonum haereses, quia eas oportebat, quasi non et malum oportuerit esse. Nam et Dominum tradi oportebat; sed vae traditori? ne quis etiam hinc haereses defendat. Si et Apellis stemma retractandum est, tam non vetus et ipse quam Marcion institutor et praeformator ejus: sed lapsus in foeminam desertor continentiae marcionensis, ab oculis sanctissimi magistri Alexandriam secessit; inde post annos regressus non melior, nisi tantum qua jam non marcionites, in alteram foeminam impegit, illam virginem Philumenen, quam supra edidimus, postea vero immane prostibulum et ipsam, cujus energemate circumventus, quas ab ea didicit phaneroseis scripsit. Adhuc in saeculo supersunt qui meminerint eorum, etiam proprii discentes et successores ipsorum, ne se posteriores negare possint. Quanquam et de operibus suis, ut dixit Dominus, revincuntur. Si enim Marcion Novum Testamentum a Vetere separavit, posterior est eo quod separavit; quia separare non posset, nisi quod unitum fuit. Unitum ergo ante quam separaretur, postea separatum, posteriorem ostendit separatorem. Item Valentinus, aliter exponens, et sine dubio emendans, hoc omnino quicquid emendat, ut mendosum retro, anterius fuisse demonstrat. Hos ut insigniores et frequentiores adulteros veritatis nominamus. Caeterum et Nigidius nescio quis, et Hermogenes, et multi alii qui adhuc ambulant pervertentes vias Dei, ostendant mihi ex qua auctoritate prodierunt. Si alium Deum praedicant, quomodo ejus Dei rebus et litteris et nominibus utuntur adversus quem praedicant? si eumdem, quomodo aliter? Probent se novos apostolos esse: dicant Christum iterum descendisse, iterum ipsum docuisse, iterum crucifixum, iterum mortuum, iterum resuscitatum: sic enim Apostolos solet facere, dare illis praeterea virtutem eadem signa edendi, quae et ipse. Volo igitur et virtutes eorum proferri; nisi quod agnosco maximam virtutem eorum, qua Apostolos in perversum aemulantur: illi enim de mortuis vivos faciebant, isti de vivis mortuos faciunt.
pass_a_gloss: Where then was Marcion, the Pontic shipmaster, a student of Stoic philosophy? Where was Valentinus, a follower of Platonic philosophy? For it is established that they were not always so, but rather during the reign of Antoninus, and at first they believed in the Catholic doctrine in the Roman Church, under the episcopate of the blessed Eleutherius, until, because of their restless curiosity, by which they also avoided their brothers, having been ejected once and twice, Marcion, indeed, with the two hundred sestertii which he had brought to the Church, was finally relegated to perpetual separation, and they disseminated the poisons of their doctrines. Afterwards, the same Marcion, having confessed repentance, when the condition given to him occurred, was to receive peace, if he would restore to the Church the others whom he had instructed for destruction, but he was prevented by death. For it was necessary that there be heresies. Nor, however, are heresies good because it was necessary that they be, as if evil had not also been necessary. For it was also necessary that the Lord be betrayed; but woe to the betrayer? lest someone also defend heresies from this. If even the lineage of Apelles is to be retracted, so much not old and also Marcion, the founder and prefigurer of it: but having fallen into a woman, a deserter of Marcionite continence, he withdrew from the eyes of the most holy master Alexander, and from there, after years, he returned, not better, except that he was no longer a Marcionite, and he attacked another woman, that virgin Philumene, whom we mentioned above, and afterwards, indeed, a monstrous prostitute, and he, being surrounded by her energy, wrote the phaneroseis which he learned from her. There are still those in the world who remember them, also their own disciples and successors, lest they be able to deny themselves as posteriors. Although they are also overcome by their own works, as the Lord said. For if Marcion separated the New Testament from the Old, he is posterior to that which he separated; because he could not separate unless it had been united. Therefore, it was united before it was separated, and afterwards separated, showing the separator to be posterior. Likewise, Valentinus, expounding otherwise, and undoubtedly correcting, demonstrates that whatever he corrects was previously flawed. We name these men as the most notable and frequent adulterers of the truth. Moreover, I ask also Nigidius, whoever he is, and Hermogenes, and many others who still walk, perverting the ways of God, to show me from what authority they have proceeded. If they preach another God, how do they use the things and letters and names of that God against whom they preach? if the same, how do they do so otherwise? Let them prove themselves to be new apostles: let them say that Christ descended again, taught again, was crucified again, died again, was resurrected again: for thus the Apostles are accustomed to act, giving them also the power to produce the same signs which He also produced. I wish, therefore, their powers to be brought forth; unless, indeed, I recognize their greatest power, by which they emulate the Apostles in a perverse way: for they made the dead live, but these make the living dead.
pass_b_english: Where was Marcion then, that Pontic shipowner and student of Stoicism? Where was Valentinus, the follower of Platonism? The record shows they were not always what they became; they appeared around the reign of Antoninus, and at first they accepted Catholic teaching in the Roman church under the blessed bishop Eleutherius. Their restless curiosity drove them on, a curiosity that even made their fellow believers avoid them, until they were expelled not once but twice. Marcion, who had brought two hundred sestertii to the church, was finally consigned to permanent separation, and the pair proceeded to spread the poison of their doctrines.

Later Marcion confessed repentance and, meeting the condition imposed on him, was to receive peace if he restored to the church the others he had taught for destruction; but death cut him off first. It was necessary for heresies to exist. That does not make heresies good, as if evil were not also necessary. The Lord had to be betrayed, yet woe to the betrayer; let no one cite this necessity to defend heresy.

If we must trace the line of Apelles, he is no more ancient than Marcion, his founder and forerunner. Apelles fell for a woman, abandoned Marcionite continence, and fled from the eyes of the most holy master Alexander to Alexandria. Years later he returned, no better, except that he was no longer a Marcionite, and he fastened onto another woman, the virgin Philumene, whom I mentioned earlier. She turned out to be a monstrous prostitute, and, caught in her spell, he wrote the phaneroseis he learned from her.

People still alive remember these men, including their own disciples and successors, so they cannot deny being their heirs. Even their own works convict them, as the Lord said. If Marcion separated the New Testament from the Old, he is later than what he separated; he could not separate them unless they had first been united. United before, separated after, the separator is shown to be the later party. Likewise Valentinus, by expounding differently and 'correcting,' proves that whatever he corrects was flawed beforehand. These are the most prominent and frequent adulterers of the truth.

Then there are Nigidius, whoever he is, Hermogenes, and many others still walking about perverting God's ways. Let them show me from what authority they sprang. If they preach another god, how do they use that god's own things, letters, and names against the very one they preach? If they preach the same God, how do they do it differently? Let them prove they are new apostles: let them say Christ descended again, taught again, was crucified again, died again, rose again. That is how the apostles operated, and they received power to work the same signs he did. I want to see their powers produced; unless, of course, you count their supreme power, by which they perversely imitate the apostles: the apostles made the dead live, these men make the living dead.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Latin text, including the complex conditional regarding Marcion's repentance and the logical argument regarding the separation of the Testaments. Pass A preserves the clause structure and specific theological distinctions (e.g., 'it was necessary that there be heresies' vs 'evil had not also been necessary'). Pass B provides a fluent rendering that maintains the agency and meaning of the original. Scripture references (implied 'as the Lord said') are handled correctly in both.
